claims.text: A machine-learning approach based on a genetic algorithm can design intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-weight RHEA compositions.
The genetic algorithm uses a population size of 100.
The genetic algorithm runs for 1000 generations.
The genetic algorithm uses a mutation rate of 0.01.
The genetic algorithm uses a crossover rate of 0.5.
Candidate compositions are constrained to have density below 8 g/cm^3.
Candidate compositions are constrained to have yield strength above 1000 MPa.
Candidate compositions are constrained to have elongation at break above 10%.
Atomic-scale crystal structure and lattice distortion mediate the effects of composition optimization.
Machine-learning-driven composition optimization can balance solid-solution strengthening, precipitation hardening, and grain-boundary strengthening.
The optimized RHEA is predicted to have a yield strength of 1200 MPa.
The optimized RHEA is predicted to have an elongation at break of 15%.
The optimized RHEA is predicted to have a density of 7.5 g/cm^3.
Conventional Ti-6Al-4V has a yield strength of 900 MPa.
Conventional Ti-6Al-4V has an elongation at break of 10%.
Conventional Ti-6Al-4V has a density of 4.5 g/cm^3.
The optimized RHEA is limited to between three and five principal elements.
The machine-learning model's accuracy may depend on the quality of its training data.
The machine-learning model's accuracy may depend on the quantity of its training data.
The genetic optimization may converge to a local optimum rather than the global optimum.

contradictions.description: The design constraint requires elongation strictly above 10%, whereas the falsification rule rejects only values below 10%; an observed elongation of exactly 10% would violate the design constraint but would not falsify the hypothesis.

The absolute falsification thresholds are not reconciled with the additional 5% prediction-error threshold. For example, a measured property could satisfy the absolute target while differing from the prediction by more than 5%, leaving the stated decision rule ambiguous.
